data.name: Muhannad
data.gender_notes: Muhannad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is given a pledge or covenant. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'ahd' meaning covenant or pledge. Muhannad is a title given to those who have taken a pledge or vow to Allah, and is often used to describe those who have completed the Hajj pilgrimage. The name Muhannad carries the meaning “Warrior” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muhannad usually hope their child will grow to embody warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to remain steadfast in your faith and commitments.
data.etymology: Muhannad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muhannad total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: مُحَنَّد
in_arabic.long_meaning: مُحَنَّد: اسم علم عربي، مشتق من الحنادة، التي تعني المنعقد، وبالتالي معناه المنعقد، أو المنحمد؛ وفي بعض الأحيان، يعني المنحمد للنبي، وذلك لانجاز المهمة، وتنفيذ الأوامر، وبالتالي، يعبر عن الشخص الذي يتمتع بالقدرة على تنفيذ الأوامر، والمساهمة في تنفيذها، والتحKir من خلاله.

historical_references.reference: Muhammad ibn Abdullah, known as Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyah or Muhannad, was the eldest son of Imam Ali and Fatimah bint Muhammad, the Prophet's daughter. He was born in Medina around 600 CE and was a prominent figure in the early Islamic community, especially in Kufa, Iraq. He is considered a Shia imam and is revered for his scholarly pursuits and piety. Muhannad died in 652 CE during the Battle of Al-Harra, a rebellion against the Umayyad Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic community, Shia imam, scholarly pursuits, piety, Battle of Al-Harra

historical_references.reference: Al-Muhannad ibn Sabah, also known as Hasan-i Sabbah, was the founder of the Nizari Ismaili movement in the 11th century CE. He is believed to have lived in Persia and Syria, and is famous for his role in the Assassins' sect. The name 'Muhannad' is a title given to him by his followers, meaning 'the Guided One'. Al-Muhannad is said to have led a secretive and mystical community, using political assassinations as a means to bring about social change.
historical_references.context: Founder of the Nizari Ismaili movement, Assassins' sect, secretive and mystical community, political assassinations
